Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic forecast errors and derive correction rules.

## Example 1 (2025-08-20)
History: Price range ~70.68 to 73.21 (volatility ~3.5)
Model forecasts: Start at 71.04, end at 74.91
True outcomes: Start at 71.29, end at 75.25

Looking at the divergence:
- At horizon 0: Model 71.04 vs True 71.29 (underestimate by ~0.25)
- The model appears to be too low compared to true values

Let me look at the pattern more carefully:

Model forecast 30d: [71.04, 71.98, 71.63, 71.05, 71.45, 70.96, 70.35, 71.24, 71.95, 71.30, 72.20, 72.45, 72.68, 73.47, 73.11, 73.14, 71.40, 71.40, 72.11, 72.65, 72.19, 73.06, 72.91, 71.98, 72.85, 72.63, 72.99, 73.79, 75.25, 74.91

True outcomes: [71.29, 72.62, 72.53, 72.19, 72.75, 72.24, 71.72, 72.99, 73.97, 73.61, 74.95, 75.44, 76.04, 77.17, 76.90, 77.10, 75.54, 75.77, 76.75, 77.51, 76.98, 77.84, 77.55, 76.21, 76.79, 76.02, 75.76, 75.98, 76.79, 75.72]

Observations:


I notice a consistent pattern of underprediction across multiple dimensions. The model consistently underestimates both current and future prices, with differences ranging from 0.2 to 2.5 units.
